clue.text: Fleet of foot, as a buck may be?

definitions.meaning: describes someone quick on their feet, a speedy runner
a dollar made quickly and easily, often dishonestly, is described with this adjective

explanation.definitionFit: A synonym of speedy, and the adjective in the idiom for money made quickly and without scruple.

clue.text: Leave club in cab — sail out!

indicators.note: the club is placed inside the rearranged letters that follow it
out can mean astray or wrong, so the two words before it are disarranged

parts.note: a bat is a club for striking a ball

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to leave their golf club in a taxi and go off sailing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave' looks like an instruction to abandon something but is a noun, time off work. 'out' gives the jumble SABICAL, which 'in' then splits open.
explanation.definitionFit: A period of paid time away from work, especially for an academic, is one kind of leave.

clue.text: Setback regarding drinks for the speaker

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: whoever speaks the word gives its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: an animal laps when it drinks with its tongue

explanation.surface: A hold-up concerning refreshments laid on for whoever is giving the talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A return to a worse state after improvement, as in an illness, is a reverse in one's progress.

clue.text: Admitting viewpoint, theologian was suspended

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the theologian lets the viewpoint inside

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree
an angle is a point of view on a matter

explanation.surface: A divinity scholar who conceded someone's point was barred from his post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspended' reads as disciplined, barred from office, but here it is literal: hung in the air. 'Admitting' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that hung loosely from above did exactly this, a literal synonym.

clue.text: African scam — travel east to take in the French

parts.note: a con is a swindle

indicators.note: to take in is to absorb, so the travel-and-east pair absorbs the French word

parts.note: to go is to travel
E is the compass abbreviation for east
les is the plural of the in French

explanation.surface: A swindle on the continent requires heading east to fool the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take in' suggests deceiving, echoing the scam, but 'to take in' is the container signal, and 'the French' asks for a French word.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Congo is an example of someone from that continent.

clue.text: Vanya, for example, regularly called on one in Paris

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it

parts.note: un is French for one

indicators.note: regularly asks for every other letter of the word after it

explanation.surface: Someone like Vanya often dropped in on a friend living in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Chekhov's play makes Vanya the best-known example of this male relative.

clue.text: Gain acceptance for popular doctor delayed in race

parts.note: to sell an idea is to win people over to it
in means fashionable
GP is a general practitioner, a British family doctor
late means behind time

explanation.surface: Winning approval for a well-liked medic who got held up while competing.
explanation.walkthrough: In British horse racing this is a low-grade contest after which the winner must be offered at auction.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a type of horse race, one whose winner is auctioned afterwards.

clue.text: Something blown by girl when crossing street …

parts.note: Penny is a girl's name, short for Penelope

indicators.note: to cross is to go over or span, so the word for when spans the street

parts.note: while can mean when, as in during the time that

explanation.surface: A girl puffs out something, perhaps a bubble, as she walks over the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheap tin flute played by breathing into it, so an instrument of the wind kind.

clue.text: … a comparatively adroit-sounding girl

indicators.note: sounding says the phrase before it is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: neat can mean deft, so more adroit is neater

explanation.surface: Following on, another girl who seems rather more skilful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comparatively' asks for the comparative form, neater, and 'sounding' gives its non-rhotic British pronunciation, written NITA.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, so an example of what a girl may be called.

clue.text: Judge resistance in a short time on ship

indicators.note: in places the resistance inside the two-word phrase after it

parts.note: a bit is a little while, as in wait a bit
R is the physics symbol for resistance
re means on the subject of
SS is the prefix for a steamship

explanation.surface: Assess how well the crew will hold out during a brief spell aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judge' reads as a verb but is a noun. 'in' puts R inside A BIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who settles disputes between parties, a female umpire or adjudicator.

clue.text: Wine-shop sinking money in marriage feast venue

indicators.note: sinking the money into the venue means burying it inside that word

parts.note: Cana in Galilee is where Jesus turned water into wine at a wedding
tin is old British slang for money

explanation.surface: A drinks seller invests cash in a place that hosts wedding receptions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sinking' reads as investing, but it buries one word in another. The venue is the Galilean village of the biblical wedding where water became wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar or shop selling wine in Spanish- and Italian-speaking countries.

clue.text: Husband leaves Gulf State, securing good deal

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so the trimmed state holds the letter for good
the husband leaves, so his letter departs from the state's name

parts.note: Bahrain is an island kingdom in the Persian Gulf
H is the genealogical abbreviation for husband
G is the abbreviation for good, as on a coin grading

explanation.surface: A married man quits the Gulf after landing a lucrative contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good deal' wants to be read together; only 'deal' defines. 'leaves' takes H from BAHRAIN giving BARAIN, and 'securing' puts G inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An agreement struck between two parties, a synonym in the sense of a transaction.

clue.text: Donut newly cooked in atypical way

indicators.note: cooking changes the form of ingredients, so the two words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A freshly fried doughnut prepared by an odd recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb meaning in a manner that is not customary or habitual.

clue.text: Make an impact as an archer?

definitions.meaning: to have a marked effect, as when the strain begins to show
William, the legendary Swiss bowman who shot an apple from his son's head, has this surname

explanation.definitionFit: A verb for having a noticeable effect, and the surname of the Swiss crossbow hero of legend.

clue.text: Prediction favouring English players

parts.note: for means in favour of
the cast are the actors, the players, in a production

explanation.surface: A pundit's tip that leans towards the England team.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement of what is expected to happen, as with the weather, is a synonym.

clue.text: Stupid going around hospital department on tiptoe?

indicators.note: the word for stupid goes round the outside of the department

parts.note: silly means foolish
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A dazed person creeps about a hospital ward on the tips of their toes.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking on one's toes is a typical way of moving without making a noise, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Corpse finally found under murder victim's tree

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece found under another comes below it

parts.note: Abel was killed by his brother Cain in Genesis, the first murder victim

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A body is at last discovered beneath a tree belonging to the dead man.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the white poplar, one species of tree.

clue.text: Shout about press chief with female associate

indicators.note: the shout goes about, that is around, the two pieces that follow

parts.note: to bellow is to shout loudly
Ed is short for editor, the head of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A row breaks out over a newspaper boss and his woman colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'female associate' reads as one phrase, but female is a separate abbreviation and only 'associate' defines; 'about' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A close companion or ally, often an unlikely one, is a synonym in the figurative sense.

clue.text: Unhappy guest wrote it around noon? It's hard to say

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the letter for noon
unhappy suggests upset or disturbed, so the three words after it are disordered

explanation.surface: A disgruntled visitor penned a note at about midday, though nobody is sure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's hard to say' sounds like a shrug of doubt, but is literal: difficult to pronounce. 'Unhappy' gives the jumble TOGUETWISTER, which 'around' wraps about noon's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase such as she sells sea shells, built to be difficult to pronounce quickly.

clue.text: State business importing India's cotton fabric

indicators.note: to import is to bring in, so the state and business bring the letter inside

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California
Co is short for company
I is the international vehicle code for India

explanation.surface: A government-run trading firm brings in cloth made in India.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain woven cloth made of cotton, originally from Calicut in India.

clue.text: Large snake? It's something different on board!

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
the adder is Britain's only venomous snake

explanation.surface: A huge serpent turns out to be quite another creature once aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The board is that of a children's game where snakes send a counter down and these send it up, so each is the other's opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: In the children's dice game it is the counterpart of the snake, taking counters upward instead.

clue.text: Build-up of anti-abortion allowance?

parts.note: pro-life is the label campaigners against abortion use
a ration is a fixed allowance of something

explanation.surface: The growth of state payments designed to discourage terminations.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapid increase in number, as with weapons, is a synonym of growth.

clue.text: Third of signs correctly sited outside a pretentious pub

indicators.note: third of asks for letter number three of the word after it
the phrase for correctly sited goes outside the letter that follows

parts.note: something in place is positioned where it should be

explanation.surface: One in three signboards is properly positioned in front of a showy bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaudily decorated Victorian drinking house, so a showy sort of tavern.

clue.text: Anger shown by second driver's supporter in cheap accommodation

indicators.note: shown by means placed beside, here after, the pieces that follow

parts.note: a tee holds the ball up for a driver, the golf club used for long shots
rage is violent anger

explanation.surface: The backup chauffeur's assistant fumes at the budget lodgings provided.
explanation.walkthrough: The driver is a golf club, not a motorist: the peg that props the ball up for it is a TEE.
explanation.definitionFit: The part of a passenger ship offering the lowest fares and most basic berths.

clue.text: Peculiar friend locking up Cockney woman's child

indicators.note: to lock up is to confine, so the friend confines the two pieces that follow

parts.note: a pal is a friend
her, a woman's, said by a Cockney, a working-class Londoner who drops initial aitches, is 'er
a son is one's child

explanation.surface: An odd acquaintance imprisons the youngster of an East End lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peculiar' reads as strange but means belonging to one individual, as in peculiar to him. 'locking up' is the container signal; Cockneys drop the aitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Something particular to one individual and nobody else is peculiar to them, a synonym in that sense.

clue.text: Language of companion in premiership team

indicators.note: in places the companion inside the team's name

parts.note: Man U is the short name of Manchester United, an English Premier League football club
CH is Companion of Honour, a British award

explanation.surface: The way a team-mate talks in a top-flight football side.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tungusic tongue of north-east China, so one example of a language.

clue.text: Fish popular at present with millions

indicators.note: with joins the pieces, the millions going alongside, here in front of, the others

parts.note: in means fashionable
now means at the present time

explanation.surface: A seafood dish that is currently a hit with vast numbers of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A small freshwater member of the carp family, so one kind of fish.

clue.text: Tower identified in Ruth — and Ezekiel ultimately?

parts.note: Babe Ruth was the famous American baseball player

indicators.note: ultimately picks the closing letter of the name before it

explanation.surface: A tower is eventually spotted in two books of the Old Testament.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruth and Ezekiel look like books of the Bible, where the tower is in fact found in Genesis; Ruth is the baseball star's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: The Genesis story names the structure built to reach heaven after this place.
